ops.title: BUG (owner decision): cc-guides check/render is broken by the .toml capt-hook fragment target — blocks committing any cc-guides change
ops.body:
**Symptom:** `cc-guides render` (and CI's `cc-guides check`, which renders all targets to compare) aborts with:
`cc-guides: layout dir ".claude/fragments/.claude/capt-hook.toml": target ".claude/capt-hook.toml" must end in .md, .sh, .json, .yml, or .yaml: unsupported extension: ".toml"`.

**Impact:** every commit that touches a cc-guides fragment/artifact reds the **Guides** CI check (the check job "could not run — layouts, lock, and fragments disagree"; the re-render job is skipped). Commits that touch NO cc-guides files pass (the check skips the full render). So cc-guides changes are effectively un-landable through the gate until this is fixed. Surfaced 2026-07-19 by a legitimate ruff-pin bump commit (2f4a1257) — the bump is correct; the red is this pre-existing bug, not the bump.

**Root cause:** `.claude/fragments/.claude/capt-hook.toml/layout.toml` (added 2026-07-18 ~10:04) composes `.claude/capt-hook.toml` from `cc-skills:capt-hook-{base,python,cc-notes}` (github:yasyf/cc-skills@main). But cc-guides only emits `.md/.sh/.json/.yml/.yaml` — a `.toml` output target is unsupported by cc-guides 0.1.29 (the latest release; CI installs it too).

**Why not force-fixed (owner decision needed):** the three options all have costs — (a) remove the `.claude/fragments/.claude/capt-hook.toml/` fragment dir and hand-maintain `.claude/capt-hook.toml` (undoes the intentional fragment-composition setup, possibly a concurrent session's/bootstrap's WIP); (b) bump cc-guides to a `.toml`-supporting version (none exists — 0.1.29 is latest); (c) change the target extension (breaks capt-hook, which requires `.toml`). Whoever set up the capt-hook fragment composition (or the cc-guides maintainer) should decide: either drop capt-hook.toml from cc-guides management, or add `.toml` support to cc-guides.

**Interim state:** commit 2f4a1257 ("bump ruff v0.8.6 → v0.15.20 for py314") carries a red Guides check for this reason; the ruff bump itself is correct and needed (the old pin couldn't parse py314, blocking every Python commit through prek). The daily scheduled Guides re-render would also fail on this until fixed.
